items.stem: Who pleads for Oedipus?
options: Antigone
sister Ismene
King Theseus
Creon of Thebes

items.stem: What do the elders do when they learn who Oedipus is?
options: Order him to leave the land at once
Crown him as their honoured guest today
Ignore the name he has just given them
Offer him a public civic welcome now

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's request: “Let me not suffer for my _____.”
options: anger
silence
confidence
riches

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's challenge: “How keep you then your _____?”
options: anger
troth
silence
weapon

items.stem: Why do the elders fear Oedipus?
options: His name and story are known and feared
He is armed when they first find him there
He is a spy sent into Attica this very day
He carries a visible plague-spot even now

items.stem: When do the elders shout “Begone”?
options: When he names himself the hapless Oedipus
When Antigone first takes him by the hand
When he asks to sit down on the rock
When he prays aloud to great Poseidon

items.stem: What is Antigone's argument in lines 243–244?
options: No one escapes ruin if a god drives him
Oedipus is innocent of every charge they name
The elders are being cruel for its own sake
Athens must take its orders from Thebes now

items.stem: What promise do the elders give before they know who Oedipus is?
options: No man shall drive him hence against his will
He may rule as king of this local deme
They will hide him from all Theban searchers
They will restore his sight before the day ends

items.stem: What name do the elders give the still-unseen trespasser during the hunt?
options: A godless man
A crowned guest of the city
A priest of the grove already
A herald sent from Theseus

items.stem: Complete the elders' direction: “And sit thee crouching on the _____ edge.”
options: level
scarped
crowded
distant

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's cry: “Woe on my fate _____!”
options: unblest
unseen
unmoved
unsaid

items.stem: When does Oedipus say he has no country?
options: When they ask his birth and home
When they offer him a civic crown
When they bring him a bowl of water
When they first call him a wayfarer

items.stem: What does Antigone mainly ask the elders to grant?
options: That father and daughter not be forced to leave
That Oedipus be crowned at once in the sacred grove
That she be sent home at once without her father
That the sacred grove itself be cut down today

items.stem: What do the elders say about requiting ill with ill?
options: Heaven’s justice does not punish it
It offends the grove's own goddesses
Only kings may repay a personal wrong
It brings a sudden plague on the land

items.stem: What do the elders still say after they pity father and daughter?
options: They cannot take back what they have already said
They will arm the whole city to drive him out
They now believe he is wholly innocent after all
They will make him a citizen of the deme at once

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's warning: “Dread my _____.”
options: city
lineage
weapon
voyage

items.stem: Complete the description of the offerings: “Bowls of spring water mingled with sweet _____.”
options: poison
sand
ashes
mead

items.stem: Immediately after Oedipus says “The hapless Oedipus,” what do the elders do?
options: They cry out and order father and daughter away
They offer him a seat of honour in the grove at once
They send a runner to fetch the local king now
They ask him to lead them in a public prayer

items.stem: What is Oedipus trying to do when he answers their questions about birth and home by saying he has no country?
options: He is withholding the name that he already dreads to speak
He is claiming Athens as his new and legal homeland now
He is denying that he ever had any parents at all
He is asking them to invent a birth-story on the spot

items.stem: What does it show that the elders can say they pity Antigone and her father and still refuse to unsay their decree?
options: Pity does not, in this scene, outweigh their fear of Heaven’s decree
They have decided the pair are lying about all of their distress
They now think the grove itself has already been wholly destroyed
They are waiting only for the local king to dismiss the pair

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's condition: “O Sirs, if I come forth at your _____,”
options: request
command
silence
ransom

items.stem: Complete Antigone's plea: “Who ’scapes perdition if a god _____!”
options: pardon
impel
comfort
delay

items.stem: What does Oedipus mean by “Ears to the blind, they say, are eyes”?
options: He locates the approaching men by hearing, not by sight
He claims that the elders have already lost their vision
He is asking Antigone to stop speaking for him now
He wants the chorus to close their ears to his name

items.stem: The chorus enters with “Ha! Where is he? Look around! / Every nook and corner scan!” What kind of entrance is this?
options: A search for a trespasser, not a hymn of welcome
A formal hymn in praise of all the local gods
A legal hearing already opened by the local king
A victory-song for a battle just now completed

items.stem: After saying they pity father and daughter, the elders add, “We cannot say aught other than we said.” What does that close show?
options: They will not unsay the decree, even while they admit pity
They have forgotten what they promised him earlier on
They now intend to crown him as a local patron saint
They are asking Antigone to speak the whole decree for them

items.stem: Which statement best captures how this parodos defines the conflict?
options: A name already feared outweighs a promise the elders have just given
The elders welcome the stranger as soon as they first learn his name
Antigone turns against her father and openly takes the elders' side
The scene is mainly a debate about who should hold the Theban throne
